excludedSourceRows.sourceIssueReference: Below you’ll find a complete chronology for Magneto comic books throughout Marvel history, including alternate realities where he played an essential role like Age of Apocalypse and House of M.
excludedSourceRows.reason: Boundary framing prose, not an issue-bearing clause.

excludedSourceRows.sourceIssueReference: Greg Pak and Carmine Di Giandomenico bring Magneto’s tragic childhood to life, showing his Jewish family’s suffering in Nazi Germany.
excludedSourceRows.reason: Commentary only; it does not name a unique issue occurrence.

excludedSourceRows.sourceIssueReference: The Jack Kirby and Stan Lee Uncanny X-Men kick off with a bang, and Magneto as the X-Men’s archnemesis right out of the gate!
Len Wein, Chris Claremont, Dave Cockrum, and John Byrne ressurect the X-Men, as well as Magneto, elevating Marvel’s merry mutants to the most popular comic in the universe.
excludedSourceRows.reason: Explanatory prose, not an issue-bearing clause.

excludedSourceRows.sourceIssueReference: Grant Morrison and Frank Quitely’s run on X-Men from 2001 to 2004 will make more sense taken as a whole, but these are the primary Magneto issues.
excludedSourceRows.reason: Publication years are commentary, not issue references.

excludedSourceRows.sourceIssueReference: Claremont returns to Excalibur for a new series featuring Professor X and Magneto.
Magneto’s relationship with Scarlet Witch takes center stage, as Marvel sets up the House of M.
Magneto rules the world! What could go wrong?
Magneto returns to a familiar role as mega villain of the X-Men.
Magneto’s role is largely tied to his place as the father of the Scarlet Witch.
Avengers vs. X-Men has major ramifications for Magneto, both for his place with the X-Men and his abilities.
